{{Short description|British mathematician (born 1953)}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=October 2020}}
[[File:Martin T. Barlow Oberwolfach 2016.jpg|thumb|Barlow at [[Mathematisches Forschungsinstitut Oberwolfach|Oberwolfach]] in 2016]]
'''Martin Thomas Barlow''' [[Royal Society#Fellows|FRS]] [[Royal Society of Canada|FRSC]] (born 16 June 1953 in [[London]]) is a British [[mathematician]] who is professor of mathematics at the [[University of British Columbia]] in [[Canada]] since 1992.<ref name=debrett/>

==History==
Barlow is the son of Andrew Dalmahoy Barlow (1916–2006) and his wife Yvonne.<ref name=dpot>{{cite book | title=Debrett's People of Today | year=2011 | page=87 | url=http://www.exacteditions.com/exact/browse/455/1210/7772/3/123 }}</ref> He is thus the grandson of [[Alan Barlow]], and his wife [[Nora Barlow|Nora (née Darwin)]], through whom he is a great-great-grandson of [[Charles Darwin]]. He is the nephew of [[Horace Barlow]] (also FRS and Fellow of Trinity).  In 1994 he married Colleen McLaughlin.<ref name=dpot/>

He was educated [[Sussex House School]], [[St Paul's School, London]], [[Trinity College, Cambridge]] (BA 1975, Diploma 1976, ScD 1993); [[University College of Swansea]] (PhD).<ref name=debrett>{{Cite web |url=http://www.debretts.co.uk/people/biographies/browse/b/25222/Martin%20Thomas+BARLOW.aspx |title=Prof Martin Barlow Authorised Biography – Debrett's People of Today, Prof Martin Barlow Profile |access-date=21 May 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110927025504/http://www.debretts.co.uk/people/biographies/browse/b/25222/Martin%20Thomas+BARLOW.aspx |archive-date=27 September 2011 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name=dpot/>

Barlow worked as a research fellow of the [[University of Liverpool]] 1978–1980.  He was a Fellow of [[Trinity College, Cambridge]], 1979–1992.  He worked in the [[Statistical Laboratory, University of Cambridge]] 1981–1985 and was a Royal Society University Research Fellow 1985–1992.<ref name=debrett/>

==Work==
His mathematical interests include [[probability]], [[Brownian motion]] and [[fractal sets]].

His doctoral students include [[Steven Neil Evans|Steven N. Evans]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=44866|name=Martin Thomas Barlow}}</ref>

==Recognition==
He was awarded the [[Rollo Davidson Prize]] in 1984.<ref name=debrett/><ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.statslab.cam.ac.uk/Rollo/award.html | publisher=[[Statistical Laboratory, University of Cambridge]] | accessdate=2011-05-26 | title=Rollo Davidson Awards 1976 - 2010 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111220062731/http://www.statslab.cam.ac.uk/Rollo/award.html | archive-date=20 December 2011 | url-status=dead }}</ref> He was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society of Canada]] in 1998.<ref name=debrett/> He was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] in 2005.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://royalsociety.org/about-us/fellowship/fellows/ | publisher=[[Royal Society]] | title=Fellows of the Royal Society | accessdate=2011-05-26 }}</ref> In 2012 he became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2012-11-03.</ref> In 2018 the [[Canadian Mathematical Society]] listed him in their inaugural class of fellows.<ref>{{citation|url=https://cms.math.ca/MediaReleases/2018/Fellows|title=Canadian Mathematical Society Inaugural Class of Fellows|publisher=Canadian Mathematical Society|date=7 December 2018|access-date=7 January 2020|archive-date=22 January 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210122125232/https://www2.cms.math.ca/MediaReleases/2018/Fellows|url-status=dead}}</ref>
